ingredientSections.heading: Black Barley Risotto
items: 1½-2 Cups Morel Mushrooms, cleaned, fresh or rehydrated (shiitake or chanterelles are good alternatives)

methodSections.heading: Brining and Roasting the Pork Shoulder
steps: Combine all the ingredients in a large pot, bring to a boil, and stir until the salt has dissolved and ingredients are well incorporated.
Allow to cool to room temperature. Fully submerge the pork shoulder, using a plate or similar to weigh down if necessary, and let marinate for a minimum of 24 hours.

Remove the shoulder from the brine and wrap tightly in several layers of aluminium foil. Place on a pan in an oven preheated to 180°C (350°F) and roast for 3½ to 4 hours. The internal temperature should be at least 85°C (190°F) after this time.
Remove from oven but keep wrapped and allow the shoulder to rest for 20 to 25 minutes.
When ready to serve, cut into portions, brush with the pork glaze (see below) and roast under the broiler set to high for 7 to 9 minutes.

methodSections.heading: Pork Glaze
steps: Heavily char the leek, tomatoes, onion, and chillies on the grill and then roughly chop.
Place in a large pot along with all the remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil and then lower the temperature and simmer until the volume of the liquid has reduced by roughly two thirds.
Remove the cinnamon stick and discard. Place the mixture into the blender and puree.
Pour through a fine strainer.
Makes about 1 litre of glaze and is great with other cuts of meat. Store in the fridge or freeze.

methodSections.heading: Onion Soubise
steps: Finely slice and then sweat the onions in a saucepan over a medium heat with the butter and bay leaves until translucent.
Deglaze with the white wine, add the cream and reduce by half.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Remove bay leaves and then puree in a blender.

methodSections.heading: Puffed Sorghum
steps: Heat the canola oil in a deep saucepan until it reaches 180°C (355°F).
Add the sorghum to the oil, after a moment it will pop not unlike popcorn, but with less vigour.
Remove the popped sorghum with a slotted spoon and place on paper towel.
Transfer to a bowl and toss with the dry ingredients.

methodSections.heading: Black Barley Risotto
steps: In a medium sized saucepan over a medium heat, sweat the garlic and shallots in a small splash of oil until they become translucent.
Add the black barley and toast in the pan for 3 to 4 minutes. After a minute or two add the mushrooms.
Deglaze with the white wine and reduce by half. Add the bay leaves and half of the chicken stock to the barley.
Bring to a boil and reduce heat to a simmer, add the rest of the stock gradually as it cooks off and is absorbed. This will take 20-25 minutes.
When tender reduce the liquid until the pan is almost dry then remove from the heat and discard the bay leaves.
Incorporate the butter a little at a time, add the herbs and lemon zest and adjust the seasoning.

methodSections.heading: Pickled Kohlrabi
steps: Combine all the ingredients except the kohlrabi into a small saucepan and bring to a boil.
Add the kohlrabi to a mason jar and pour the hot brine over the top.
Once at room temperature it can be stored in the fridge.

methodSections.heading: Plating & Garnishes
steps: Plate in proportions and in a design that inspires you.
Garnish with celery curls, radishes, pea tendrils, sunflower shoots and a soft poached egg.
